en.headline: Educators and experts urge stronger regulation of social media for under-16s
en.dek: Calls for legislation or tighter rules to curb addiction and cyberbullying among children intensified on Saturday, with a survey showing majority public support and think-tank suggestions for targeted controls rather than a blanket ban.
body: Educators, lawmakers and researchers on Saturday renewed calls for Hong Kong to introduce stronger regulation of social media use by children under 16, citing addiction, cyberbullying and mental-health risks.

Lilian Chan Lui Ling-yee, honorary president of the Yan Oi Association of Principals, said social media addiction was the biggest problem facing education and that legislation was needed to protect the next generation. She described addiction as irreversible and said a ban would raise public awareness of harmful content.

A survey by New Youth Forum of 686 adults found 61.8 per cent supported legislation restricting under-16s from social media, rising to 76.3 per cent among parents. Ray Poon of the PoD Research Institute said a blanket ban might not be viable, but controls on infinite scroll, personalised advertising and overnight notifications could reduce addictive elements, alongside better guidelines for parents and schools.

Poon noted challenges faced by places that have already imposed restrictions, including young people using VPNs or parental accounts to bypass rules. The government has previously indicated it has no immediate plan for a legislative ban but remains open to issuing guidelines.

zh.headline: 教育界及專家倡加強規管16歲以下使用社交媒體
zh.dek: 周六教育界、議員及智庫再呼籲加強規管未成年使用社交平台，指成癮及網絡欺凌問題嚴重，民調顯示逾六成市民支持立法限制16歲以下使用。
body: 教育界、議員及研究人員周六再呼籲本港加強規管16歲以下兒童使用社交媒體，以應對成癮、網絡欺凌及精神健康風險。
仁愛堂校長聯會名譽會長陳呂令宜表示，社交媒體成癮是教育面對的最大問題，必須立法保障下一代。她形容成癮「不可逆轉」，立法可提高公眾對有害內容的意識。
新青年論壇一項調查訪問686名成年市民，61.8%支持立法限制16歲以下使用社交媒體，家長支持度更高達76.3%。智庫PoD Research Institute研究總監潘智謙表示，全面禁止未必可行或必要，但可考慮規管無限滾動、個人化廣告及夜間通知等成癮元素，並為家長及學校提供更好指引。
潘智謙指已實施限制的地區面對年輕人用VPN或父母帳戶繞過規則等挑戰。政府早前表示暫無立法禁止計劃，但對發出指引持開放態度。
